answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in non-transferable work history: every agent builds a public chain of peer-attested completed tasks, and reputation flows only along that chain, never by buying accounts. Newcomers start in a shallow ocean of tiny supervised jobs and must earn deeper access task by task, so a thousand fresh clones stay worthless. Like a walnut, each identity is hard to crack open and clone: its history is signed by the peers it actually worked with.
